title: Thermal Properties of Matter
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Thermal Properties of Matter Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_code: O-Level Physics (6091): Thermal Properties of Matter
standard_text: Describe a rise in temperature of an object in terms of an increase in its internal energy; define heat capacity and specific heat capacity and apply Q = mcΔθ; describe melting, boiling and evaporation in terms of the kinetic particle model and explain why the temperature stays constant during a change of state; define specific latent heat of fusion and vaporisation and apply Q = mL; distinguish between boiling and evaporation and describe the factors that affect evaporation and its cooling effect (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on thermal properties of matter: internal energy, heat capacity, specific heat capacity, latent heat, heating curves, boiling and evaporation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Temperature stays constant during a change of state.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heating raises the internal energy of a body.

  • Q = mcΔθ: c is the specific heat capacity, in J/(kg °C). Heat capacity C = Q ÷ Δθ, in J/°C.
  • Q = mL during a change of state: L is the specific latent heat of fusion (melting) or vaporisation (boiling), in J/kg.
  • While a substance melts or boils, the energy breaks forces between particles, so the temperature stays constant (flat parts of a heating curve).
  • Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature and cools the liquid; it is faster when hotter, with more surface, with wind and in dry air.
Example

Energy to heat 2 kg of water by 15 °C? (c = 4200)

Q = 2 × 4200 × 15

Answer: 126 000 J

Example

Energy to melt 0.5 kg of ice? (L = 334 000 J/kg)

Q = 0.5 × 334 000

Answer: 167 000 J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the temperature rises while ice melts. It stays at 0 °C until all the ice has melted.
  • Mixing up heat capacity (whole object, J/°C) and specific heat capacity (per kg, J/(kg °C)).
  • Using Q = mcΔθ during a change of state. Use Q = mL there.
  • Calling boiling and evaporation the same.

faq.q: What is the difference between heat capacity and specific heat capacity?
faq.a: Heat capacity is the energy to raise a whole object by 1 °C (J/°C). Specific heat capacity is the energy to raise 1 kg of the substance by 1 °C (J/(kg °C)).

faq.q: Why are there flat parts on a heating curve?
faq.a: During melting and boiling, the energy supplied overcomes the forces between particles (latent heat), so the temperature does not rise.

faq.q: What affects the rate of evaporation?
faq.a: Temperature, surface area, air movement (wind) and humidity. Hotter, larger, windier and drier all make evaporation faster.

items.q: Why does a sandy beach get hotter than the sea on a sunny day?
c: Sand has a much lower specific heat capacity than water.
items.e: Same energy, bigger temperature rise for sand.

items.q: How is boiling different from evaporation?
c: Boiling happens only at the surface.
Boiling happens throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature; evaporation happens only at the surface at any temperature.
items.e: Bubbles of vapour form inside a boiling liquid.

c: The most energetic particles escape, so the average kinetic energy of the particles left behind falls.
items.e: This is why sweating cools you.
